comparison_boundary: Independent client and server processes on loopback using the same zero-byte echo handler. Bare Axum has no transport policy; axum_transport adds the same request ID, sensitive header, body/head, response header, and concurrency policy class; bridge adds a bounded single-owner dispatch; lenso includes immutable Host admission in the resolved Plan, bounded live connections and HTTP/2 streams, header/body/idle deadlines, Web Ingress, Kernel invocation, and the native Endpoint Module.

source.benchmark_source: Commit b3ff552 (PR #36), based on base_repository_commit, with bounded Ingress resources, a low-overhead hot path, and Host-owned admission alignment.

measurement_notes.latency: p50 and p99 are sequential unloaded keep-alive request latency, not coordinated-omission-safe loaded latency.
measurement_notes.cpu_and_memory: CPU percent and RSS KiB are peak samples from ps during a separate workload with the same request count, so sampling does not alter the reported throughput samples.
measurement_notes.saturation: The one-second client deadline is long enough for sixteen waves at the shared 32-request admission ceiling; HTTP rejection or client timeout therefore indicates a scheduling or admission failure rather than the expected bounded wait.
measurement_notes.repeatability: The immediately preceding full run of the same optimized binary measured policy Axum at 100304 requests/s and Lenso at 93556 requests/s with 8 connections, or 93.27%. The recorded final run measured 92.61%; both restore the pre-change ratio range without weakening limits.
measurement_notes.scope: One host sample is decision evidence, not a product performance guarantee.

decision.finding: The remaining material imbalance is HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connection affinity in the Ingress coordinator: one hot connection uses one lane, while two or more connections distribute evenly. Bounded Host admission now completes 512 delayed requests without rejection or timeout.
decision.next_boundary: If production traces show a small number of hot or multiplexed connections, investigate request/stream-aware Ingress routing, lane health, and load selection before changing Kernel scheduling. Reconsider a separate Web execution profile only after repeated feature-equivalent workloads remain materially limited after that boundary is addressed.
